As sojourners and exiles, they were to abstain from the passions of the flesh, which wage war against the soul, and to keep their conduct honorable among unbelievers, so that others would see their good deeds and glorify God.
Peter's message is our message too.
We are living far from our true home, but we are not homeless.
Our inheritance is waiting, and our hope is alive.

vocab.vi: Người lưu vong, kẻ xa xứ
Khách tạm trú, người ở tạm
Của sở hữu; dân thuộc về
Điều tuyệt vời, đức tính cao đẹp

questions.q: 1. To whom did Peter write, and where were they living?
questions.a: To Christians scattered across Asia Minor, living far from home as strangers in the cities where they lived.

questions.q: 2. What three words describe the believers' inheritance in 1 Peter 1:4?
questions.a: Imperishable, undefiled, and unfading.

questions.q: 3. Who guards the believers while they wait, and how?
questions.a: God guards them by his power through faith (1 Peter 1:5).

questions.q: 4. What four things does Peter call believers in 1 Peter 2:9?
questions.a: A chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, and a people for God's own possession.

questions.q: 5. Why must believers keep their conduct honorable among unbelievers?
questions.a: So that when others speak against them as evildoers, they may see their good deeds and glorify God on the day of visitation (1 Peter 2:12).

passages.title: Bài 2: Đau Khổ và Hy Vọng
sentences: Paul wrote Romans 8 to Christians who were suffering.
He did not tell them that their suffering was small, and he did not tell them that God had forgotten them.
He told them something far greater: the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory that is to be revealed to us.
Paul looked at the whole creation and saw it groaning, like a woman in the pains of childbirth, waiting to be set free from its bondage to corruption.
We groan inwardly too, as we wait for the redemption of our bodies.
Hope is not pretending that everything is fine.
Hope is waiting with patience for what we do not see yet.
While we wait, the Spirit helps us in our weakness.
When we do not know what to pray for as we ought, the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words.
And we know that for those who love God, all things work together for good, for those who are called according to his purpose.
Paul then asked the question that every suffering Christian asks: Who shall separate us from the love of Christ?
Shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?
His answer is a shout of victory: No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us.

Neither death nor life, nor angels nor rulers, nor things present nor things to come, nor powers, nor height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
James agrees.
He tells us to count it all joy when we meet trials of various kinds, because the testing of our faith produces steadfastness.
Suffering does not separate us from God.
It proves that his love holds us, even in the dark.

vocab.vi: Sự nô lệ, ách trói buộc

questions.q: 1. What does Paul compare present sufferings with in Romans 8:18?
questions.a: The glory that is to be revealed to us — present sufferings are not worth comparing with it.

questions.q: 2. What is the whole creation doing, according to Romans 8:22?
questions.a: It has been groaning together in the pains of childbirth, waiting to be set free from its bondage to corruption.

questions.q: 3. How does the Spirit help us when we do not know what to pray?
questions.a: He intercedes for us with groanings too deep for words (Romans 8:26).

questions.q: 4. What does James say the testing of faith produces?
questions.a: Steadfastness — the testing of faith produces steadfastness (James 1:3).

questions.q: 5. Name four things Paul says cannot separate us from the love of God (Romans 8:38-39).
questions.a: Any four of: death, life, angels, rulers, things present, things to come, powers, height, depth, anything else in all creation.

passages.title: Bài 3: Sự Khôn Ngoan Cho Quyết Định
sentences: Every day we make decisions, and some of them change our lives.
Shall I take this job?
Shall I move to another city?
Shall I marry this person?
The Bible does not give us a list of answers for every decision, but it does give us a way to decide.
Solomon wrote the shortest guide to decisions in the whole Bible: Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.
In all your ways acknowledge him, and he will make straight your paths.
Trusting God does not mean we stop thinking.
It means we do not trust our thinking alone.
We bring our plans to God, we ask him for wisdom, and we let him straighten the path.
James tells us how to ask: If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask God, who gives generously to all without reproach, and it will be given him.
God does not scold us for asking.
He gives generously, like a father who loves to give good gifts.
But James adds a warning: let him ask in faith, with no doubting.
The person who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind, a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.
And James gives us a test for every decision: the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial and sincere.
A decision that comes from God will look like that list.
It will be pure, not mixed with selfish ambition.
It will be peaceable, not full of quarrelling.
It will be gentle and open to reason, not proud and stubborn.
So when you face a hard decision, do not decide alone and do not decide in a hurry.
Ask God for wisdom, talk to wise friends, and wait for peace.
The straight path is the path God makes straight.

vocab.vi: Hòa thuận, yêu chuộng hòa bình

questions.q: 1. What two commands does Proverbs 3:5 give?
questions.a: Trust in the Lord with all your heart, and do not lean on your own understanding.

questions.q: 2. What does God promise if we acknowledge him in all our ways (Proverbs 3:6)?
questions.a: He will make straight our paths.

questions.q: 3. According to James 1:5, how does God give wisdom?
questions.a: He gives generously to all without reproach.

questions.q: 4. What happens to the person who doubts, according to James 1:6-8?
questions.a: He is like a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind; he is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways (James 1:6-8).

questions.q: 5. Name four qualities of the wisdom from above (James 3:17).
questions.a: Any four of: pure, peaceable, gentle, open to reason, full of mercy and good fruits, impartial, sincere.

passages.title: Bài 4: Tâm Trí Của Cơ Đốc Nhân
sentences: Paul begins Romans 12 with an appeal: I appeal to you therefore, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your spiritual worship.
Worship is not only what we do on Sunday.
It is what we do with our bodies, our time, and our minds every day.
Then Paul tells us how change happens: Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind.
The world has a pattern, and it presses us into its shape every day — through the news, through advertising, through the opinions of people around us.
We do not change by trying harder in our own strength.
We change when our minds are renewed, and our minds are renewed by what we feed them.

That is why Philippians 4:8 gives us a filter for every thought: Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever is honorable, whatever is just, whatever is pure, whatever is lovely, whatever is commendable, if there is any excellence, if there is anything worthy of praise, think about these things.
Eight qualities, one question: is this thought true, honorable, just, pure, lovely, commendable, excellent, and worthy of praise?
If it is not, do not let it dwell in your mind.
A renewed mind can do what an unrenewed mind cannot: it can discern what is the will of God, what is good and acceptable and perfect.
So guard your mind the way you would guard a house.
Choose what comes in through the door.
Read God's word first in the morning.
Meditate on what is true.
And watch what happens: the mind that is renewed is the mind that is transformed.

vocab.vi: Cư ngụ, ở lại lâu trong tâm trí
Bị bắt giữ, bị khống chế

questions.q: 1. What does Paul appeal to believers to do in Romans 12:1?
questions.a: To present their bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is their spiritual worship.

questions.q: 2. How are we transformed, according to Romans 12:2?
questions.a: By the renewal of our minds.

questions.q: 3. What will a renewed mind be able to do?
questions.a: Discern what is the will of God: what is good and acceptable and perfect.

questions.q: 4. Name four things Philippians 4:8 tells us to think about.
questions.a: Any four of: true, honorable, just, pure, lovely, commendable, excellent, worthy of praise.

questions.q: 5. Why does it matter what we feed our minds?
questions.a: Because what we think about shapes who we become — we are transformed by what fills our minds, so we must guard what we feed them.

passages.title: Bài 5: Lãnh Đạo và Phục Vụ
sentences: Jesus called his disciples together and taught them a lesson about leadership that turned the world upside down.
You know, he said, that those who are considered rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and their great ones exercise authority over them.
That is how the world leads: from above, by power, by force.
But it shall not be so among you.
Whoever would be great among you must be your servant, and whoever would be first among you must be slave of all.
For even the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
Jesus did not only teach this; he lived it.
He washed feet, he carried a cross, and he gave his life.
The greatest leader in history was the greatest servant in history.
Paul gives the same teaching in practical form when he lists the qualities of an overseer.
The saying is trustworthy: If anyone aspires to the office of overseer, he desires a noble task.

Therefore an overseer must be above reproach, the husband of one wife, sober-minded, self-controlled, respectable, hospitable, able to teach, not a drunkard, not violent but gentle, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money.
Notice what is missing from the list: Paul does not ask for a great speaker, a rich man, or a popular leader.
He asks for character.
He must manage his own household well, with all dignity keeping his children submissive, for if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he care for God's church?
What happens at home shows what will happen in the church.
He must not be a recent convert, or he may become puffed up with conceit and fall into the condemnation of the devil.
Moreover, he must be well thought of by outsiders, so that he may not fall into disgrace, into a snare of the devil.
So the church should choose servants, not kings.
It is the servant who is truly great, and it is the gentle leader whom God blesses.

vocab.vi: Người giám sát (trưởng lão, mục sư)

questions.q: 1. How do Gentile rulers lead, according to Mark 10:42?
questions.a: They lord it over people; their great ones exercise authority over them.

questions.q: 2. What must the greatest among believers be (Mark 10:43-44)?
questions.a: The greatest must be the servant; the first must be slave of all.

questions.q: 3. Why did the Son of Man come, according to Mark 10:45?
questions.a: Not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.

questions.q: 4. What does 1 Timothy 3:1 say about desiring to be an overseer?
questions.a: It is a noble task.

questions.q: 5. Why must an overseer not be a recent convert?
questions.a: He may become puffed up with conceit and fall into the condemnation of the devil (1 Timothy 3:6).

passages.title: Bài 6: Truyền Giáo Trong Thế Giới Đa Nguyên
sentences: Paul came to Athens, the most famous city of learning in the ancient world, and he found a city full of idols.
The people of Athens worshipped many gods, and they were so careful not to miss one that they had built an altar with the inscription: To the unknown god.
Paul stood in the midst of the Areopagus and began, not with an attack, but with respect: Men of Athens, I perceive that in every way you are very religious.
For as I passed along and observed the objects of your worship, I found also an altar with this inscription.
What therefore you worship as unknown, this I proclaim to you.
Paul found common ground, and then he proclaimed the truth.

The God who made the world and everything in it, being Lord of heaven and earth, does not live in temples made by man, nor is he served by human hands, as though he needed anything, since he himself gives to all mankind life and breath and everything.

This God made from one man every nation of mankind to live on all the face of the earth, having determined allotted periods and the boundaries of their dwelling place, that they should seek God, and perhaps feel their way toward him and find him.
Yet he is actually not far from each one of us, for in him we live and move and have our being.
Paul even quoted their own poets: For we are indeed his offspring.
Although many people in Athens worshipped many gods, Paul showed them the one true God.
On the other hand, he never forced anyone.
He reasoned, he persuaded, and he left the result to God.

Peter gives the same rule to us: in your hearts honor Christ the Lord as holy, always being prepared to make a defense to anyone who asks you for a reason for the hope that is in you; yet do it with gentleness and respect.
Be ready with a reason, and give it gently.
That is evangelism in a pluralist world: respectful, clear, and gentle, leaving the result to God.

vocab.vi: A-rê-ô-pa (nơi họp nổi tiếng ở A-thên)
Lời biện hộ, sự bảo vệ

questions.q: 1. What did Paul find in Athens (Acts 17:23)?
questions.a: An altar with the inscription: To the unknown god.

questions.q: 2. What does Paul say about the God who made the world (Acts 17:24-25)?
questions.a: He is Lord of heaven and earth; he does not live in temples made by man; he gives to all mankind life and breath and everything.

questions.q: 3. Why did God make all nations, according to Acts 17:26-27?
questions.a: That they should seek God, and perhaps feel their way toward him and find him.

questions.q: 4. What did Paul quote from the Athenians' own poets (Acts 17:28)?
questions.a: 'In him we live and move and have our being' and 'For we are indeed his offspring.'

questions.q: 5. How should we give a defense of our hope, according to 1 Peter 3:15-16?
questions.a: With gentleness and respect, having a good conscience.
